CVE-2009-20002.title: Millenium MP3 Studio <= 2.0 .pls File Stack-Based Buffer Overflow
CVE-2009-20002.description: Millenium MP3 Studio versions up to and including 2.0 is vulnerable to a stack-based buffer overflow when parsing .pls playlist files. The application fails to properly validate the length of the File1 field within the playlist, allowing an attacker to craft a malicious .pls file that overwrites the Structured Exception Handler (SEH) and executes arbitrary code. Exploitation requires the victim to open the file locally, though remote execution may be possible if the .pls extension is registered to the application and opened via a browser.

CVE-2026-123638.title: Gitea protected file pattern bypass with quoted file names
CVE-2026-123638.description: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

CVE-2026-125272.title: BIG-IP APM Vulnerability
CVE-2026-125272.description:
Description:

When BIG-IP APM is licensed and provisioned, and a virtual server with the APM access profile is configured with a per-request policy containing a form-based Logon Page, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate.

Impact:

Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-62162.title: Hydra: Deposit Claim omits Head state-token spending requirement
CVE-2026-62162.description: Hydra is a layer-two scalability solution for Cardano. Prior to 2.1.0, the `Claim` branch in `hydra-plutus/validators/deposit.ak` checks only that `datum.head_id` matches the attacker-controlled `redeemer.currencySymbol` and that the transaction is valid before the deposit deadline. It neither requires spending the Head state-token UTxO in the same transaction nor constrains outputs. After a deposit made through `POST /commit` is confirmed, any third party able to build a Cardano transaction can observe and consume the pending deposit UTxO before its deadline and redirect the assets to an arbitrary address. A standalone deposit spend invokes no Head validator, bypassing its safety checks; historical head-ID binding and the Aiken rewrite retained this missing invariant. The default deadline is three times depositPeriod, so the described attack applies to pending deposits before that deadline. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.0.

pps: generators: fix use-after-free when closing a removed device

device_release+0xca/0x3c0
kobject_put+0x169/0x320

sched/fair: Clear throttle state when leaving the fair class

Task-based CFS bandwidth throttling removes a task's fair sched_entity
while the scheduler core still considers the task queued. p->throttled
carries the fair-specific state across dequeue/enqueue operations.

fair enqueue with p->throttled still set.

remains set, and put_prev_task_fair() places the entity in the EEVDF tree
while the task moves to RT. On exit, the fair picker can select the

net/sched: clamp skb->queue_mapping before indexing the tx queue

This issue was caught by Sashiko (nipa). A producer-side path cap is

CVE-2026-99713.title: KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure
CVE-2026-99713.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure

Conditionally reschedule when retrying a guest PTE walk because the CMPXCHG
to update A/D bits failed, e.g. because a different task/vCPU modified the
relevant gPTEs. On kernels without involuntary preemption of some kind, a
misbehaving guest can "capture" a pCPU effectively indefinitely and trigger
soft lockups by continuously modifying its gPTEs such that the result of
the walk is remains valid.
